chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀṣim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who does not find water, so he performs tayammum and stands in salat, then a servant comes and says, 'Here is the water.' He said: 'If he has not bowed in rukuʿ, then let him turn away and perform wudu (ablution); but if he has bowed, then let him continue in his salat.'

key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمَ: he performed tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.فَلْيَنْصَرِفْ: he should leave or break off the prayer
key_terms.يَرْكَعْ: he performs the bowing position of rukuʿ

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if water is found after beginning salat with tayammum?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who begins salat with tayammum because water is unavailable, then finds water during the prayer. If he has not yet reached rukuʿ, he should leave the prayer and perform wudu (ablution), but if he has already bowed in rukuʿ, he should continue his salat.
